family: Indian family dynamics often involve strict parenting, comparison with peers (e.g., 'Sharma ji ka beta'), emphasis on respect for elders, taunts about marriage or career, close-knit joint family structures, and sibling banter (bhai/behen).
education: Intense societal and parental pressure on academic excellence in India, prioritizing Engineering/Medical, rote learning, report card anxiety, board exam hype, and tuition classes.
college: College life in India involves mandatory 75% attendance rules, internal exams, KT/backlogs, placement and campus interview anxiety, hostel life, mess food struggles, and canteen hangouts.
JEE/exams: JEE, NEET, UPSC, and government exams in India. Coaching hubs like Kota, Allen, intense competition, sleepless nights, rank race, and cutoffs are frequent satirical themes.
cricket: Cricket is a religion in India. Frequent memes feature MS Dhoni (Thala, helicopter shot), Virat Kohli (chase master), Rohit Sharma, IPL rivalries (CSK vs MI, RCB 'Ee Sala Cup Namde'), and umpire decisions.
Bollywood: Bollywood movies, iconic dialogues and meme templates (e.g., Baburao, Raju, Shyam from Hera Pheri, Munna Bhai, Gangs of Wasseypur, 3 Idiots), dramatic acting, and superstar personas (SRK, Salman, Akshay).
food: Obsession with chai/tea (cutting chai, biscuits), street food (pani puri/golgappa, momos, samosa, chole bhature), midnight Maggi, paneer vs non-veg debates, and bargaining with vegetable vendors.
festivals: Diwali (deep cleaning, soan papdi forwarding, firecracker bans), Holi (color attacks, gujiya), Raksha Bandhan (pocket money draining), Eid, and Durga Puja.
marriage/wedding: Big fat Indian weddings, arranged marriage matrimonial Biodata, nosy relatives asking 'shaadi kab karoge?', buffet food rush, dowry and extravagant ceremonies.
relationships: Conservative societal attitudes towards dating, sneaking calls from parents, 'nibba-nibbi' cringe teenage romance tropes, breakups, friendzones, and eternal bachelorhood (singlehood).
workplace: Corporate IT/office culture in India: demanding bosses, unpaid weekend overtime, appraisal disillusionment, 90-day notice periods, HR activities vs real hikes, and Work From Home challenges.
social_norms: 'Log kya kahenge' (What will people/society say?), aggressive bargaining, Jugaad (creative improvised hacks), superstition (nimbu-mirchi), and relative comparison.
regional_culture: Regional stereotypes and city traits: Delhi winters/smog/aggression ('Tu janta hai mera baap kaun hai'), Mumbai local trains and monsoons, Bengaluru traffic and startup tech-bro jargon, Bihar UPSC aspirants.
daily_life: Middle-class life tropes: bargaining with auto/rickshaw drivers, meter refusal, power cuts, IRCTC tatkal ticket booking panic, reusing plastic dabbas, and saving money.
hindi_slang: Desi slang, conversational fillers, and street expressions (e.g., 'Arey yaar', 'Bawa', 'Bhau', 'Chai-sutta', 'Bakchodi', 'Scene kya hai', 'L lag gaye', 'Gajab bezzati hai', 'Mast plan hai'). Often used for comedic hyperbole and expressive informal tone.
internet_culture: Viral Indian internet memes, YouTuber references (CarryMinati, BB Ki Vines), viral catchphrases ('Binod', 'Rasode me kaun tha', 'Pawri hori hai', 'Ruk jaa bhai', 'Choti bacchi ho kya'), and Desi Reddit/Instagram meme templates.
religion: Cultural traditions, rituals, festive fasting (vrat), temple visits, prasad, and respectful mythological references.
other: Miscellaneous Indian pop-culture and internet memes.
